Package com.lemarketjames.common.audit

Class AuditRecorder

java.lang.Object
com.lemarketjames.common.audit.AuditRecorder
@Service public class AuditRecorder extends Object
The only way to write the audit trail (contract C2). Each service records the lifecycle events it causes, so audit never waits on another feature.

The rule "an event is written in the same transaction as the change it describes" is enforced, not just documented: Propagation.MANDATORY makes a call from outside a transaction fail, and inside one the event commits or rolls back together with the change.

    • record

      @Transactional(propagation=MANDATORY) public void record(AuditEventType type, Integer orderId, Integer accountId, Map<String,Object> details)
      Records one event for an order.
      Parameters:
      type - what happened
      orderId - the order it happened to
      accountId - the order's account; the client id is resolved from it
      details - the keys documented on type

    • recordSubmission

      @Transactional(propagation=MANDATORY) public void recordSubmission(SubmissionAuditEvent event)
      Records one event of an order submission. Its SubmissionAuditEvent.eventKey() is unique in the table, so writing the same event again fails and rolls the caller's transaction back instead of storing a duplicate.
